description:
Observed at run bd-review-loop-20260517T193724Z-3658183 (epic JMAP-x2gd). The loop completed iter 1 cleanly: /do-beads landed 8 commits + 8 closes; verdict block emitted 'genuine convergence: no findings filed this pass' and 'borderline: only P3+ findings, no opinion labels' (both branches firing is itself odd — log shows both messages back-to-back); summary persisted final_verdict=genuine_convergence as bd metadata.

Then stderr emitted:
  /home/mark/bin/bd-review-loop: line 625: syntax error near unexpected token `fi'

`bash -n /home/mark/bin/bd-review-loop` reports the script is syntactically clean. Line 625 is inside the post-loop MAX_RUNTIME check, but MAX_RUNTIME was unset so that branch shouldn't fire. The error is probably coming from a sub-command (cost_exceeds, count_findings, an awk/jq invocation, or date arithmetic) whose output gets eval'd or executed and produces the parser error.

The bug is cosmetic — verdict and metadata were written correctly and convergence detection worked — but it makes a successful run look like a failure to a casual reader and would mask a real script crash if one ever happened.

Also worth investigating: the double-log of two mutually-exclusive verdict branches ('genuine_convergence' and 'low_priority_only / borderline') in the same iter. The if/elif chain at lines 597-610 makes them mutually exclusive; both firing suggests stale variables across a subshell boundary, or the script took both branches via subshell control flow. Same vicinity as the syntax error.

Repro: any /do-beads-only iteration that exits without filing new findings under bd-review-loop --epic <id>.
title: bd-review-loop: spurious 'syntax error near unexpected token fi' at line 625 after successful convergence
